g.text: N1 [Context]
LLMs grow in size and compute cost
As Large Language Models (LLMs) have grown in popularity and size, they have
begun consuming a non-trivial amount of compute and time for training and
inference (Kim et al. (2023), Pope et al. (2022)).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) As Large Language Models (LLMs) have grown in popularity and size, they have begun consuming a non-trivial amount of compute and time for training and inference (Kim et al. (2023), Pope et al. (2022)).

g.text: N2 [Context]
Adaptive compute methods speed up inference
Adaptive compute methods seek to speed up the inference stage of
Transformers (Vaswani et al. (2023)), the de facto LLM architecture, by
identifying and avoiding redundant computations to save I/O and
floating-point operations (FLOPs).
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=1) Adaptive compute methods seek to speed up the inference stage of Transformers (Vaswani et al. (2023)), the de facto LLM architecture, by identifying and avoiding redundant computations to save I/O and floating-point operations (FLOPs).

g.text: N3 [Prior_Work]
Neuron adapters target MLP layers
Commonly, these methods apply neuron adapters to the Multi Layer Perceptron
(MLP) layers of the Transformer architecture, which dynamically ignore
neurons depending on the input of the layer (Lee et al. (2024), Mirzadeh et
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=4) Commonly, these methods apply neuron adapters to the Multi Layer Perceptron (MLP) layers of the Transformer architecture, which dynamically ignore neurons depending on the input of the layer (Lee et al. (2024), Mirzadeh et al. (2023), Liu et al. (2023) Zhang et al. (2024)).

g.text: N4 [Prior_Work]
Speedup: O(d_in d_hidden) -> O(d_in d_adapted)
Utilizing these adapters leads to inference speedups, as the amortized time
complexity of an MLP layer reduces from O(din ·dhidden ) to O(din ·dadapted
), where din is the input dimension of the MLP, dhidden is the hidden
dimension, and…
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Utilizing these adapters leads to inference speedups, as the amortized time complexity of an MLP layer reduces from O(din ·dhidden ) to O(din ·dadapted ), where din is the input dimension of the MLP, dhidden is the hidden dimension, and dadapted is the average number of active neurons.

g.text: N5 [Prior_Work]
Neuron adapters: practical speedup, small quality drop
For modern Transformer architectures, this results in practical speedups at
the expense of negligible model quality decrease for a sufficient amount of
average active neurons.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) For modern Transformer architectures, this results in practical speedups at the expense of negligible model quality decrease for a sufficient amount of average active neurons.

g.text: N6 [Limitation]
Rapid performance drop on modern Transformers
Unfortunately, adaptive compute methods using neuron adapters suffer from
rapid performance degradation in modern Transformer architectures (Figs. 1a,
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) Unfortunately, adaptive compute methods using neuron adapters suffer from rapid performance degradation in modern Transformer architectures (Figs. 1a, 1c).

g.text: P6 [Proof]
Fig. 1a, 1c: degradation evidence
Figs. 1a, 1c
g.title: P6 [Proof] (cites=0) Figs. 1a, 1c

g.text: N7 [Limitation]
Root cause: activation-based allocation
We observe this issue arises from the limitations of the neuron-adaptive
framework, which enforces dynamic neuron allocation based on activation
values.
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) We observe this issue arises from the limitations of the neuron-adaptive framework, which enforces dynamic neuron allocation based on activation values.

g.text: N8 [Limitation]
Three concrete limitations
Concretely, we believe this decline is attributed to this framework's lack
of generalization across different layer types, reliance on sparse
activation functions, and costly neuron masking techniques.
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) Concretely, we believe this decline is attributed to this framework's lack of generalization across different layer types, reliance on sparse activation functions, and costly neuron masking techniques.

g.text: N8a [Limitation]
Cannot apply to QKV / non-MLP layers
First, neuron adapters, often tailored to MLPs, can not be
directly applied to non-MLP layers, such as the Query, Key, and
Value modules of attention layers, which lack neurons.
g.title: N8a [Limitation] (cites=0) First, neuron adapters, often tailored to MLPs, can not be directly applied to non-MLP layers, such as the Query, Key, and Value modules of attention layers, which lack neurons.

g.text: N8b [Limitation]
Depends on activation sparsity (ReLU only)
In addition, these methods frequently depend on activation-induced
sparsity, like that attained by ReLU (Agarap (2019)), making them
ineffective with non-sparse activation functions like SwiGLU
(Shazeer (2020), Zhang et al. (2024)).
g.title: N8b [Limitation] (cites=3) In addition, these methods frequently depend on activation-induced sparsity, like that attained by ReLU (Agarap (2019)), making them ineffective with non-sparse activation functions like SwiGLU (Shazeer (2020), Zhang et al. (2024)).

g.text: N8c [Limitation]
CATS/ReLUfication: costly pre-activation compute
Further, while recent approaches like CATS (Lee et al. (2024)) or
ReLUfication (Mirzadeh et al. (2023)) attempt to handle non-sparse
activations, they inefficiently compute neuron-activations before
determining which neurons to exclude.
g.title: N8c [Limitation] (cites=2) Further, while recent approaches like CATS (Lee et al. (2024)) or ReLUfication (Mirzadeh et al. (2023)) attempt to handle non-sparse activations, they inefficiently compute neuron-activations before determining which neurons to exclude.

g.text: N9 [Limitation]
Modern LLMs use non-sparse activations
This is concerning as Transformers architectures like Llama (Touvron et al.
(2023)), Gemma (Team et al. (2024)) or Mistral (Jiang et al. (2023)) rely on
non-sparse activation functions, which makes sparsity-based neuron adapters…
g.title: N9 [Limitation] (cites=3) This is concerning as Transformers architectures like Llama (Touvron et al. (2023)), Gemma (Team et al. (2024)) or Mistral (Jiang et al. (2023)) rely on non-sparse activation functions, which makes sparsity-based neuron adapters ineffective for them, pushing us to rely on more computationally intensive neuron adapters.

g.text: N10 [Method]
Propose Adaptive Rank Allocation + RaNA
To address these gaps in the neuron-adaptive setup, we propose the Adaptive
Rank Allocation framework, together with the Rank and Neuron Allocator
(RaNA) adapter.
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) To address these gaps in the neuron-adaptive setup, we propose the Adaptive Rank Allocation framework, together with the Rank and Neuron Allocator (RaNA) adapter.

g.text: N11 [Method]
Rank-adaptive generalizes neuron-adaptive
We note that this rank-adaptive framework is a more powerful generalization
of the neuron-adaptive one.
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) We note that this rank-adaptive framework is a more powerful generalization of the neuron-adaptive one.

g.text: N12 [Method]
Linear(x) ≈ A(r(x) ⊙ Bx) decomposition
Concretely, we devise this framework from the observation that any linear
layer can be decomposed into the product of two low-rank matrices and an
adaptive router/masker, namely Linear(x) = W x ≈ A(r(x) ⊙ Bx).
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=0) Concretely, we devise this framework from the observation that any linear layer can be decomposed into the product of two low-rank matrices and an adaptive router/masker, namely Linear(x) = W x ≈ A(r(x) ⊙ Bx).

g.text: N13 [Method]
RaNA: A,B + masker for QKV and MLPs
Moreover, we develop RaNA in this framework, leveraging specific A and B
decompositions and a masker m(x) for Transformer layers, like QKV or MLPs.
g.title: N13 [Method] (cites=0) Moreover, we develop RaNA in this framework, leveraging specific A and B decompositions and a masker m(x) for Transformer layers, like QKV or MLPs.

g.text: N14 [Method]
Applies to any linear layer, no sparsity needed
Notably, unlike neuron adapters, RaNA can be directly applied to any linear
layer without relying on activation function sparsity.
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) Notably, unlike neuron adapters, RaNA can be directly applied to any linear layer without relying on activation function sparsity.

g.text: N15 [Method]
Better FLOP distribution across SwiGLU MLP
Further, when used with modern MLP layers with SwiGLU activations, it
enables better distribution of compute across the MLP's linear layers.
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) Further, when used with modern MLP layers with SwiGLU activations, it enables better distribution of compute across the MLP's linear layers.

g.text: N16 [Result]
Empirical validation
We empirically validate the rank-adaptive framework and the RaNA adapter.
g.title: N16 [Result] (cites=0) We empirically validate the rank-adaptive framework and the RaNA adapter.

g.text: N17 [Result]
Ranks of AB have sparse importances
We demonstrate that, similar to neuron-adaptive setups, the ranks of the AB
matrix decomposition in the proposed RaNA adapters have sparse importances,
depending on the input (Figs. 2a, 2b), allowing us to dynamically prune
them.
g.title: N17 [Result] (cites=0) We demonstrate that, similar to neuron-adaptive setups, the ranks of the AB matrix decomposition in the proposed RaNA adapters have sparse importances, depending on the input (Figs. 2a, 2b), allowing us to dynamically prune them.

g.text: N18 [Result]
Lowest MLP recovery error: +6.7/+18.1/+7.4 pp
We also show that RaNA adapters attain the lowest error in MLP layers when
recovering the full MLP outputs, outperforming neuron-adaptive methods by
6.7, 18.1 and 7.4 percentage-points on Llama2-7b, Gemma-2b and Pythia-160M
respectively.
g.title: N18 [Result] (cites=0) We also show that RaNA adapters attain the lowest error in MLP layers when recovering the full MLP outputs, outperforming neuron-adaptive methods by 6.7, 18.1 and 7.4 percentage-points on Llama2-7b, Gemma-2b and Pythia-160M respectively.

g.text: N19 [Result]
Applied to Llama and Gemma
Further, we show the effectiveness of RaNA in modern Transformer
architectures by applying it to Llama (Touvron et al. (2023)) and Gemma
(Team et al. (2024)).
g.title: N19 [Result] (cites=2) Further, we show the effectiveness of RaNA in modern Transformer architectures by applying it to Llama (Touvron et al. (2023)) and Gemma (Team et al. (2024)).

g.text: N20 [Result]
Outperforms CATS at multiple compression rates
Notably, RaNA closes the gap between full-model and adapted-model
performance, as it outperforms the state-of-the-art method CATS (Lee et al.
(2024)) on multiple compression rates (Tabs. 1, 2).
g.title: N20 [Result] (cites=1) Notably, RaNA closes the gap between full-model and adapted-model performance, as it outperforms the state-of-the-art method CATS (Lee et al. (2024)) on multiple compression rates (Tabs. 1, 2).

g.text: N21 [Result]
44% compression: +4/8 pp Llama2; +7/5 pp Gemma
Concretely, at a ∼44% FLOP compression rate, RaNA achieves an average
improvement of 4 perplexity-points and 8 percentage-points in benchmark
accuracy for Llama2-7b, while for Gemma-2b, it improves perplexity by 7
points and accuracy by 5…
g.title: N21 [Result] (cites=0) Concretely, at a ∼44% FLOP compression rate, RaNA achieves an average improvement of 4 perplexity-points and 8 percentage-points in benchmark accuracy for Llama2-7b, while for Gemma-2b, it improves perplexity by 7 points and accuracy by 5 percentage-points, compared to prior adapters.

g.text: N22 [Result]
Applied to Pythia (GPTNeoX) suite
Finally, to assess the effectiveness of RaNA's applicability to different
types of layers and activations, we apply it to the Pythia suite (Biderman
et al. (2023)), a set of varied-sized GPTNeox (Black et al. (2022)) models.
g.title: N22 [Result] (cites=2) Finally, to assess the effectiveness of RaNA's applicability to different types of layers and activations, we apply it to the Pythia suite (Biderman et al. (2023)), a set of varied-sized GPTNeox (Black et al. (2022)) models.

g.text: N23 [Result]
Pythia: better perplexity and accuracy
Here we also observe that, when comparing their performance to conventional
neuron-adaptive methods, it consistently attains better perplexity and
downstream task performance (Figs. 1c, 4).
g.title: N23 [Result] (cites=0) Here we also observe that, when comparing their performance to conventional neuron-adaptive methods, it consistently attains better perplexity and downstream task performance (Figs. 1c, 4).
